what_happened: The person running Athena read the plan on 12 Nov and saw three steward-approved jobs at places 184, 185 and 186 of 188: website records, let fresh fixes skip the old queue, and cost labels. The re-triage mechanism that landed on 11 Nov did not move them. No job failed. The person running Athena reported it and did not reorder the queue by hand.
cause: Queue order is set by age and tier. An owner or steward approval carries no weight in it. The queue has no step that turns an approval into a run, and no check that approved items rise in the plan. The re-triage mechanism that landed on 11 Nov has no test against real approved items. It was also not shown to have changed the order, so the same approved fixes still sit at the back, behind the backlog they were meant to clear.
other_causes: The item that lets fresh fixes skip the old queue is itself stuck behind that queue, so the fix for the ordering problem cannot take effect.
Approved steward items are not tracked from approval to decision to job, so nothing shows when an approved item has not become a run.
A backlog of about 188 items against a limited number of dispatches a day keeps growing, so stale and duplicate items are never retired.
open_hypotheses: The re-triage mechanism may never have been run against these items, or may rank by a field these approvals do not set.
The fields given do not show whether the mechanism is meant to move approved items at all or only to retire stale ones.
contradictions: The re-triage mechanism landed on 11 Nov at 00:51 UTC, before the cost-labels item was approved at 11:20 UTC on 12 Nov. It could not have moved that item, so that item does not show the mechanism failing.
prevention: Make approval part of queue order. An item the steward or owner has approved, and any fix for a known failure class, gets a tier ahead of ordinary requests. Cap each tier, so priority cannot inflate again. Have each drain check that every approved item is in the top N of the plan, or has a recorded job, and report any that is not. Add a test that replays the current plan and shows the three approved items moving up.
proposed_request: Make steward approval count in queue order. (1) An item the steward has approved, and any fix for a known failure class, must rank ahead of ordinary queued requests. Keep a fixed cap on how many items sit in that tier, and say which items overflow. (2) Each time the plan is built, list any approved item that is not within the first 10 places and give the reason it is not. (3) Show with a test built from the current plan that the website-records, fresh-fixes-skip-the-old-queue and cost-labels items move to the top places. Do not change the order of items that are not approved. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
